items.title: Presentations and Announcements
Karyn Boscariol, Habitat for Humanity Guelph Wellington
notes: re: Hands On For Housing Youth & Housing Conference 2024 Karyn Boscariol, Habitat for Humanity Guelph Wellington invited Members of Council to participate in the Hands On For Housing youth conference. She noted, this three-day event held at Elora’s Grand River Raceway is a unique experience provided at no cost to over 150 youth participants from local high schools in the Upper Grand and Wellington Catholic District School Boards, and select community organizations, to address the critical issue of affordable housing. K. Boscariol indicated through hands-on housing advocacy workshops, participants will develop youth-driven recommendations for the future of housing in Wellington County.
Karyn Boscariol responded to questions and noted several local skilled trade companies will be participating.

items.title: Delegations
notes: Mayor Watters, having declared a conflict of interest on item 11.2, Bissell Park Multi Use Pad, left the room and Deputy Mayor Lustgarten- Evoy assumed the Chair. Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy called upon the delegations to come forward, indicating they each have 10 minutes to address Council.

items.title: Tom Keating, on behalf of the Elora Rockers Sports Association
notes: appeared regarding agenda Item 11.2 Bissell Park Multi Use Pad, indicating their continued commitment to the project and their desire to support inclusive, safe and free play.

items.title: David Alves appeared regarding agenda Item 11.2 Bissell Park Multi
notes: Use Pad, indicating he has tended to the ice rink at the park for over 32 years and expressed his desire to have accessible and inclusive free play all year round. He noted the surface is used for more than just hockey, he has witnessed other activities such as Yoga, Zumba, puppy training classes, farmer's market, basketball, etc. He expressed his support for the staff recommended option.

items.title: Laura Carrie, resident, appeared regarding agenda Item 11.2 Bissell
notes: Park Multi Use Pad, suggesting Council pause and reflect on the environmental impact the proposed facility will have. She questioned whether this initiative aligns with the community’s commitment to environmental sustainability. She encouraged Council to consider more environmentally friendly recreational options such as investing in natural ice surfaces and supporting the community members who volunteer to flood and maintain them, enhance outdoor spaces for year round activities, expand the multi-use trails, create outdoor basketball courts and community art and garden spaces.

items.title: Macheo Carrie, resident appeared regarding agenda Item 11.2 Bissell
notes: Park Multi Use Pad suggesting the community needs outdoor recreational facilities that are inclusive, designed for all age groups, and better support the needs of youth.

items.title: Andy Abra, VP CW Celtics appeared regarding agenda Item 11.2 Bissell
notes: Park Multi Use Pad in support of facilities for youth basketball. He outlined the growing need for basketball courts to support the sport in Centre Wellington.

items.title: John Xintavelonis, resident, appeared before Council regarding Item
notes: 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions indicating he is the owner of 456 Wellington Rd 7. He respectfully requested consideration for this property to be included in the boundary expansion. He noted the property is situated along a growth corridor, adjacent to a proposed town house development and situated strategically between industrial, residential and commercial uses.

items.title: David Galbraith, Up Consulting Ltd., registered to speak regarding
notes: agenda item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions; however sent notice to the Municipal Clerk he is unable to attend.

items.title: Tom Keating, James Keating Construction appeared regarding agenda
notes: Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions seeking clarification as to the rationale for certain lands to be included while others were not included in the boundary expansion.
He questioned the vision to expand to the south of Fergus rather than focus growth between the two communities.

items.title: Robyn McIntyre, MHBC Planning on behalf of Skyway Estates Ltd.,
notes: appeared regarding agenda Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions. She indicated her client owns lands at 6686 Irvine Street, Salem also known as the North Wissler Lands. She noted the subject lands have not been included in the recommended expansion and asked that consideration be given of the North Wissler Lands for inclusion in the Salem settlement area to allow for the efficient use of existing infrastructure and allow for the rounded development of existing neighbourhoods.

items.title: Michael Puopolo, Polocorp Inc., appeared regarding agenda item 11.4
notes: Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary
Expansions. He indicated he owns 90 acres, just east of Highway 6/St.

David Street Fergus and is supportive of the inclusion of the southern portion of their holdings municipally addressed as 968 David Street North, Centre Wellington. He requested consideration for the more northerly lands at 6581 Highway 6, to also be included in the expansion area to form a consolidation of approximately 40 hectares. M. Puopolo noted these additional lands are well-suited for urban development from a locational, serviceability, transportation and cultural perspective.

items.title: Juliane von Westerholt, MHBC Planning on behalf of Elora Greens Inc.,
notes: appeared regarding agenda Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions. She indicated her client owns lands at 127 First Line which have been identified for partial inclusion within the settlement area boundary. She also indicated support for the inclusion of these lands and respectfully requested consideration for inclusion of the entire parcel to avoid fragmentation of agricultural lands and the creation of a landlocked parcel.

items.title: Ted and Marlene Buczek, 6585 Highway 6 appeared regarding agenda
notes: Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions. M. Buczek feels development of their lands adjacent to Fergus would provide much needed housing in the community and would love to provide young people an opportunity to afford a home and an opportunity to stay in the community.
James Buczek explained a desire to develop their lands with opportunities to provide much needed housing and support agricultural output through community gardens.

items.title: Michel Labbe, President & CEO Home Opportunities Non-Profit
notes: appeared before Council regarding the Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report, indicating inclusion of lands identified as 6585 Highway 6 is contiguous to the existing urban area and has access via Highway 6 to food, shelter, education, health care, arts and recreation. He noted the development of these lands would provide an appropriate mix of housing, jobs, stores, transportation options, and public service facilities for all ages and abilities. He indicated approximately 60% of the units will be affordable to annual incomes between $35,000 and $95,000 and there will be convenience commercial on Highway 6 and a multi-functional community space provided onsite.

items.title: Matthew Cory on behalf of Malone Given Parsons Ltd., appeared
notes: regarding agenda Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions. He outlined the Elora Sands Development, known as the Clayton subdivision at the southwest corner of southwest of Nichol Road 15 and Irvine Street. He respectfully requested Council consider including these lands within the urban boundary, with support from technical studies indicating this area is an ideal location for good growth.

items.title: Edward John on behalf of Tribute (Fergus Oaks) Limited c/o Landwise
notes: regarding agenda item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions did not appear and provided a written submission.

items.title: Emily Elliott, MHBC Planning on behalf of Biltmore Homes Ltd.,
notes: appeared regarding agenda Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions, property owners of 795 Anderson Street, Fergus. She requested consideration for the subject lands to be included within the Fergus Primary Urban Centre. She noted the rationale for the request, including no impact on agricultural services, adjacent to residential uses and represents a minor rounding out of the existing boundary.
E. Elliott responded to a question regarding the absence of agricultural production for more than 50 years.

items.title: Keith Reycraft, Brett Cormier, Breymark Homes and Ricard Booy
notes: appeared regarding Item 11.4 Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions. R. Booy spoke to the merits of including lands located between the Township’s new Operations Centre and property owned by Polocorp Inc., into the urban boundary. He noted a proposal to improve traffic flow and provide a second access to the new Operations Centre with a joint development venture.

items.title: Danny Trombetta, Eventus regarding agenda Item 11.4 Centre
notes: Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary Expansions did not appear and provided a written submission.

items.title: Samantha Boehmer, Elora appeared regarding agenda Item 11.4
notes: Centre Wellington Recommended Settlement Area Boundary

Expansions requesting lands at 103 Gilkinson Street be included in the expanded boundary area. She noted the 5.5 acres are not currently farmed, they are adjacent to the Granite Homes development on South River Road and ideally back onto the Cataract Trail.
Mayor Watters thanked the delegations and called a 10 minute recess.
The meeting resumed at 7:24 pm

notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services Presentation by Michael Biljetina, ATA Architects Inc.

Staff and the consultants responded to questions regarding similar facilities in Burlington and Oakville, technology for refrigerated surfaces, funding sources, monies expended on other sports facilities, and provided clarification on the grant criteria.
After a lengthy discussion, the following was put forward:
Discussion ensued and Council Members supported the suggestion that additional public consultation be carried out as well as a review of the project by the Climate Change Coordinator.

items.title: Termite Management Subsidy Program
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report seeking Council’s endorsement of the proposed Termite Management Program. He indicated the subsidy program is based on Council direction using $1.39 million dollars to facilitate program spending over a 5-year term. The program subsidy amount is based on the number of properties identified in the 2020/2021 survey data and further expanded to account for potential termite migration.
A. McNabb responded to questions regarding launch of the program, the communication strategy, plan for treatment of public spaces, and plans for public awareness and education.

Staff responded to questions regarding the future urbanization of Second Line, and the location of the employment lands.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington endorses Option 3: Bissell Park new outdoor refrigerated multi-use surface with a roof structure, including mechanical and storage buildings, as outlined in Report No. CS2024-32, at an estimated total construction and design cost of $5,700,000, contingent on a successful grant application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington endorse a grant application to the Ontario Community Sport and Recreation Fund for a request to fund 50% of the Bissell Park Multi Use Pad Project, inclusive of a new outdoor refrigerated multi-use surface with a roof structure, including mechanical and storage buildings, for the total Capital project cost of $5,700,000, and directs staff to prepare and submit the application; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington directs staff to include a top up in the 2025 Draft Capital Budget in the amount of $700,000; AND THAT Council directs staff to engage with potential community partners, service groups, and potential donors to gather commitments toward funding the budget gap between available funding and the current project deficit should the project application be successful; AND THAT Council directs staff to return to Council for further direction and consideration of the project, should the grant application be unsuccessful.
